Visually exploring data is a powerful approach to discover,
understand, and interpret novel or not-well defined patterns. It
allows us to gain insights and generate hypotheses for subsequent
analyses. However, visual exploration can become challenging when the
patterns of interest are sparsely-distributed, several orders of
magnitude smaller than the entire dataset, or detected with high
uncertainty. In this talk, I will discuss challenges in visually
exploring multi-modal and multi-scale data, and present new
visualization systems for efficiently browsing, comparing, and finding
patterns in the context of genomic, geospatial, and time-series data.
Specifically, I will describe a web platform for browsing multi-modal
and multi-scale datasets, as well as their guided navigation. I will
present a generalized framework and toolkit for interactively
arranging, grouping, and aggregating thousands of pattern instances.
And I will demonstrate how interactive visual machine learning can
enhance our ability to find patterns effectively.
